lead: Welcome. This is the short version of what the site is for — the handful of ideas the rest of it builds on. Nothing to sign up to, nothing you need to know first. Five minutes, and then you can go and have a play.

trust: Trust works better as a prediction than a feeling: from what you've seen so far, you expect a person or a tool to behave a certain way, and you change your mind when they don't. There's a well-known way of picturing it, from The Trusted Advisor by David Maister, Charles Green and Robert Galford. It goes up with whether you've shown you know your subject, whether you do what you said you would, and whether people feel safe bringing you something awkward — and down with how much you seem to be in it for yourself.

steering: Being left alone isn't the same as being in charge of what you're aiming at. AI is very good at handing you the first — it clears the chores and answers before you've finished asking — and it can quietly take the second, because the effort it saved you was the deciding. So hand over the volume, and keep the calls that carry what you actually care about.

others: Everything in your head is detailed. What you can get out of it — a sentence, a sketch, a file — is thin by comparison. So nobody ever quite receives your understanding: they get what you managed to put down, and build their own version of it. That isn't a failure on either side. It's just what two separate people are.
